name: Copper rivet reinforcement
summary: A small copper rivet set at a point of strain, such as a pocket corner or the base of a fly. The seam does not tear.
how: Find the seam that tears first under load, such as the corner of a pocket.
Punch a hole through both layers of cloth at the end of the seam.
Set a copper rivet through the hole and close it with a die.

origin.note: Jacob Davis rivets the pocket corners of work trousers, and the patent that he shares with Levi Strauss follows on 20 May 1873.

adoptions.via: The factory of Levi Strauss in San Francisco makes the riveted waist overall in denim and duck.
